papers.csv.title: ILLUSION: Unveiling Truth with a Comprehensive Multi-Modal, Multi-Lingual Deepfake Dataset
papers.csv.authors: Kartik Thakral, Rishabh Ranjan, Akanksha Singh, Akshat Jain, Mayank Vatsa, Richa Singh
papers.csv.abstract: ILLUSION is a 1.3-million-sample multimodal and multilingual deepfake dataset spanning images, audio, video, and synchronized media. Its still-image protocols separately benchmark detection and source attribution on text-to-image systems, synthetic faces, and real-world Midjourney and ArtGuru images.

papers.csv.title: Omni-IML: Towards Unified Interpretable Image Manipulation Localization
papers.csv.authors: Chenfan Qu, Yiwu Zhong, Fengjun Guo, Lianwen Jin
papers.csv.abstract: Omni-IML is a generalist localization model spanning natural images, documents, faces, and scene text, together with the Omni-273k interpretation dataset. Its natural-image protocol independently evaluates GLIDE diffusion edits in CocoGlide alongside classical manipulation benchmarks.

papers.csv.title: Image Manipulation Detection with Implicit Neural Representation and Limited Supervision
papers.csv.authors: Zhenfei Zhang, Mingyang Li, Xin Li, Ming-Ching Chang, Jun-Wei Hsieh
papers.csv.abstract: This work combines implicit-neural-representation preprocessing with weakly supervised and unsupervised manipulation detection. In addition to conventional benchmarks, it independently evaluates instruction-guided edits from IEdit and MagicBrush with image- and pixel-level metrics.

papers.csv.title: UnionFormer: Unified-Learning Transformer with Multi-View Representation for Image Manipulation Detection and Localization
papers.csv.authors: Shuaibo Li, Wei Ma, Jianwei Guo, Shibiao Xu, Benchong Li, Xiaopeng Zhang
papers.csv.venue: IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition
papers.csv.venue_name: IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition
papers.csv.raw_venue: Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition
papers.csv.abstract: UnionFormer unifies object, RGB, and noise views for concurrent image-manipulation detection and localization. Its evaluation includes CocoGlide diffusion edits and the paper's 512-image BDNIE set generated with Blended Diffusion for text-driven natural-image editing.

papers.csv.title: ForgerySleuth: Empowering Multimodal Large Language Models for Image Manipulation Detection
papers.csv.authors: Zhihao Sun, Haoran Jiang, Haoran Chen, Yixin Cao, Xipeng Qiu, Zuxuan Wu, Yu-Gang Jiang
papers.csv.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems
papers.csv.venue_name: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems
papers.csv.raw_venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems
papers.csv.abstract: ForgerySleuth combines a multimodal language model, trace encoder, and vision decoder to explain and segment manipulated regions, and introduces the ForgeryAnalysis dataset. It reports separate localization results on diffusion-edited COCOGlide and includes AutoSplice AIGC inputs.

papers.csv.title: THEMIS: Towards Holistic Evaluation of MLLMs for Scientific Paper Fraud Forensics
papers.csv.authors: Tzu-Yen Ma, Bo Zhang, Zichen Tang, Junpeng Ding, Haolin Tian, Yuanze Li, Zhuodi Hao, Zixin Ding, Zirui Wang, Xinyu Yu, Shiyao Peng, Yizhuo Zhao, Ruomeng Jiang, Yiling Huang, Peizhi Zhao, Jiayuan Chen, Weisheng Tan, Haocheng Gao, Yang Liu, Jiacheng Liu, Zhongjun Yang, Jiayu Huang, Haihong E
papers.csv.abstract: THEMIS benchmarks multimodal language models on scientific-paper fraud across seven image scenarios and five fraud types. Its AI-Generated category separately evaluates entirely generated panels and targeted generative edits with classification, localization, and set-based metrics.

papers.csv.title: ForgDiffuser: General Image Forgery Localization with Diffusion Models
papers.csv.authors: Mengxi Wang, Shaozhang Niu, Jiwei Zhang
papers.csv.venue: International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence
papers.csv.venue_name: International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence
papers.csv.raw_venue: Thirty-Fourth International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence
papers.csv.abstract: ForgDiffuser conditions a diffusion decoder on forged images to generate localization masks. Its six-dataset evaluation separately reports localization on DALL-E 2 AutoSplice and BrushNet diffusion edits as well as traditional manipulation sets.

papers.csv.title: DiffForensics: Leveraging Diffusion Prior to Image Forgery Detection and Localization
papers.csv.authors: Zeqin Yu, Jiangqun Ni, Yuzhen Lin, Haoyi Deng, Bin Li
papers.csv.venue: IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition
papers.csv.venue_name: IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition
papers.csv.raw_venue: Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition
papers.csv.abstract: DiffForensics combines frozen semantic features, denoising-diffusion pretraining, and edge-cue enhancement for image-level detection and pixel-level localization. Its evaluation separates traditional edits from deep-generative AutoSplice and OpenForensics inputs.

papers.csv.title: Towards Generic Image Manipulation Detection with Weakly-Supervised Self-Consistency Learning
papers.csv.authors: Yuanhao Zhai, Tianyu Luan, David Doermann, Junsong Yuan
papers.csv.venue: IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision
papers.csv.venue_name: IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision
papers.csv.raw_venue: Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision
papers.csv.abstract: WSCL learns weakly supervised image-level manipulation detection and produces localization maps using multi-source and inter-patch consistency. It independently evaluates language-driven editing on GIER and IEdit, both before and after image-label fine-tuning.

proposals.title: ILLUSION: Unveiling Truth with a Comprehensive Multi-Modal, Multi-Lingual Deepfake Dataset
proposals.abstract: ILLUSION is a 1.3-million-sample multimodal and multilingual deepfake dataset spanning images, audio, video, and synchronized media. Its still-image protocols separately benchmark detection and source attribution on text-to-image systems, synthetic faces, and real-world Midjourney and ArtGuru images.
proposals.version_note: The official ICLR 2025 proceedings paper is canonical; no DOI, arXiv record, or OpenAlex work was established.

proposals.original_title: ILLUSION: Unveiling Truth with a Comprehensive Multi-Modal, Multi-Lingual Deepfake Dataset
proposals.exact_unresolved_question: Does ILLUSION independently benchmark broader synthetic-image detection beyond faces, audio spoofing and talking-head/video forgeries? Identify the image subset and its separate results.

decision.decisive_evidence: Sections 3.1 and 4, Tables 5-6 and 10-11, separately evaluate still images in Set B and Set C. Set B includes SDXL, Kandinsky 2.1, and SDXL-Turbo imagery; Set C includes 20,000 Midjourney and 1,000 ArtGuru images. Table 11 reports image-source attribution separately from audio and video.
decision.narrowed_scope_rationale: The paper independently benchmarks passive detection and source attribution for fully generated, non-face still images.
decision.identity_note: The official ICLR record supplies no DOI, arXiv ID, or OpenAlex work. The normalized title, complete author list, ILLUSION acronym, 2025 venue, bounded fuzzy matches, and active exclusions were checked against the 657-paper baseline; no representation was found.

proposals.title: Omni-IML: Towards Unified Interpretable Image Manipulation Localization
proposals.abstract: Omni-IML is a generalist localization model spanning natural images, documents, faces, and scene text, together with the Omni-273k interpretation dataset. Its natural-image protocol independently evaluates GLIDE diffusion edits in CocoGlide alongside classical manipulation benchmarks.
proposals.version_note: The ICLR 2026 proceedings paper is canonical; arXiv 2411.14823 uses the earlier title 'Omni-IML: Towards Unified Image Manipulation Localization'.

proposals.original_title: Omni-IML: Towards Unified Interpretable Image Manipulation Localization
proposals.exact_unresolved_question: Which of Omni-IML’s four tasks and Omni-273k manipulation types involve generative AI edits or fully generated images, and are their forensic results reported separately?

decision.decisive_evidence: Section 4/Table 1 marks AIGC among Omni-273k manipulation types across the unified domains. Section 5/Table 2 reports natural-image localization separately on CocoGlide, a 512-image GLIDE diffusion-editing test set; the appendix preserves the per-dataset split.
decision.narrowed_scope_rationale: Generative editing is a substantive, independently scored localization condition, not merely a dataset annotation or architectural claim.

proposals.title: Image Manipulation Detection with Implicit Neural Representation and Limited Supervision
proposals.abstract: This work combines implicit-neural-representation preprocessing with weakly supervised and unsupervised manipulation detection. In addition to conventional benchmarks, it independently evaluates instruction-guided edits from IEdit and MagicBrush with image- and pixel-level metrics.
proposals.version_note: The ECCV 2024 Springer proceedings chapter is canonical; no separate arXiv version was established.

proposals.title: THEMIS: Towards Holistic Evaluation of MLLMs for Scientific Paper Fraud Forensics
proposals.abstract: THEMIS benchmarks multimodal language models on scientific-paper fraud across seven image scenarios and five fraud types. Its AI-Generated category separately evaluates entirely generated panels and targeted generative edits with classification, localization, and set-based metrics.
proposals.version_note: The ICLR 2026 proceedings paper is canonical; arXiv 2603.25089 is its preprint version.

proposals.exact_unresolved_question: Which THEMIS fraud types involve AI-generated scientific images or generative edits, and do standalone image-forensic results distinguish them from classical duplication/tampering and text reasoning?

decision.decisive_evidence: Section 3 and Appendix A.3.4 define AI-Generated panels as whole-panel Image Inference Forgery or partial Targeted Region Editing, yielding 74 fully generated and 550 partially generated verified images. proposals.original_title: DiffForensics: Leveraging Diffusion Prior to Image Forgery Detection and Localization
proposals.exact_unresolved_question: Do DiffForensics evaluation sets contain substantive generative manipulation? A diffusion pretraining prior for the detector is not sufficient evidence about the input images.

decision.decisive_evidence: Section 4.1 explicitly separates six traditional-editing datasets from AutoSplice and OpenForensics, which it identifies as deep-generative-model forgeries. decision.narrowed_scope_rationale: Deep-generative manipulations are substantive, independently scored detection/localization inputs beyond the detector's diffusion prior.

proposals.exact_unresolved_question: Do WSCL’s in-/out-of-distribution tests include generatively edited or fully generated images? Multi-source and inter-patch consistency alone do not establish generative input provenance.

decision.narrowed_scope_rationale: Language-guided generative edits receive a dedicated quantitative detection evaluation.
